title: Democracy unfolding
content: Self-organization, solidarity and the struggle for systemic change lay behind the recent defeat of Serbia’s authoritarian government. Active participants in the student movement describe their motivation and strategies for building a democratic government based on citizen participation, care and the determination to root out inequitable practices.

title: Nepsat dějiny podle vítězů
content: Vydáním České cikánské rapsodie v roce 2016 získal historik Jan Tesař nové čtenáře ještě po své osmdesátce. V žádném z politických režimů, které zažil, však nepsal příběhy v souladu s výklady minulosti, o něž se opírala moc. Platilo to i pro témata odboje a vztahu české společnosti k autoritářství.

title: History written not by the winners
content: The Czech historian and dissident Jan Tesař (1933–2025) challenged both the official communist history of the Protectorate as well as mainstream reformist historiography. All the way into his late work, he remained the model of a non-conformist historian.

title: The family as an ideological battlefield
content: Rigid, traditional and restrictive – though communicated via contemporary media language, the far right’s concept of the family remains unchanged. Questioning how Austrian Identitarians are gaining ground on debates over migration, sex education and LGBTQIA+ rights despite ongoing static membership, raises concerns over the mainstreaming of far-right discourse.

title: Praising the best of the worst
content: The memory of the civil society that emerged in western Ukraine under the auspices of the Habsburgs is still strong in the region. So too is the memory of western Ukraine’s loss of sovereignty in 1919, together with the dire repercussions this had in the following decades.
